payload.goal: Create new employee Bruno Oliveira, assign department HR, set employment details including start date, permanent employment, 100% position, annual salary 640000 NOK, and standard working hours 7.5 hours per day.
success_checks: Employee Bruno Oliveira is created with date of birth 1990-06-13
Department HR exists and employee is assigned to it
Employment start date is set to 2026-11-18
Employment type is registered as permanent employment
Standard working hours are set to 7.5 hours per day
risk_notes: PDF does not provide email, phone, address, or organization-specific employee number
Department HR may need to be created first in empty sandbox
Payroll-related salary setup may require additional fields not stated in the offer letter
Standard working hours may need conversion to weekly hours depending on API validation
Probation period and notice terms are present in the letter but may not map directly to available employee fields

extra_fields.language_hint: Portuguese request with Norwegian offer letter

ordered_steps: Check whether department HR exists; if not, create department via department endpoint
Create employee record via employee endpoint with name Bruno Oliveira and date of birth 1990-06-13
Update employee to assign department HR and job title Seniorutvikler
Configure employment details with start date 2026-11-18, employment type permanent, and position percentage 100.0
Configure salary details with annual salary 640000
Configure standard working hours as 7.5 hours per day or equivalent weekly hours if required by API
Verify employee is active and linked to the correct department and employment settings

planned_endpoints.summary: Find employees corresponding with sent data.

rules: ALWAYS search first: GET /employee?email=<email> — the sandbox often has pre-existing employees. Reuse if found.
Only POST /employee if GET returns 0 results.
When POSTing, ALWAYS include department={"id": dept_id}. Create department first if needed.
userType should be 'STANDARD' unless admin is explicitly requested.

payload.headline: Near-perfect employee creation run; one check failed, likely job title missing
what_went_wrong: Check 5 failed — likely the job title 'Seniorutvikler' was never set on the employee record; no PUT /employee/{id} call was made to update the job title field.
Two 422 errors wasted calls: first attempt used userType=STANDARD (requires email), second omitted userType entirely (required field). Should go straight to NO_ACCESS.
Two tool inspection calls (inspect_tripletex_endpoint for /employment and /employment/details) added overhead without being strictly necessary given known schema.
what_worked: All core entities created correctly: HR department, employee, employment record, employment details (100%, 640000 NOK, PERMANENT), and standard working hours (7.5h/day).
Correct endpoint sequencing: department → employee → employment → employment/details → standardTime.
what_to_try_next: After creating the employee, add a PUT /employee/{id} call to set the jobTitle field to 'Seniorutvikler' — this is likely what caused Check 5 to fail.
Use userType=NO_ACCESS directly on the first POST /employee attempt to eliminate the two 422 validation errors and reduce error count.
Remove the two inspect_tripletex_endpoint tool calls and the initial GET /department check if department name is known from the task — saves ~3-4 calls for efficiency bonus.
unnecessary_calls: POST /employee with userType=STANDARD — should have used NO_ACCESS immediately, this call always fails without email
POST /employee with no userType — redundant retry before finding correct value, adds another 422 error
inspect_tripletex_endpoint calls for /employee/employment and /employee/employment/details — schema was already known from planning
